title: Chemical commitment: distinguish hydrolysis protection, replacement damage and actual wrong-bond selectivity
status_authority: Actual version-bound scoped internal review governs acceptance. Source reports, mathematical verification and physical acquisition remain separate.

scientific_scope_status: Postbond rejection can improve conditional purity without restoring original-root yield: with correct/wrong irreversible attempt probabilities p,w and ideal readers, correct L-step yield is at most[p/(p+w)]^L. Endless iid false reads of a persistent wrong product eventually admit it. Complete donor-owned reset and no premature chemistry give precommit wrong/correct odds (lambda_W/lambda_C)*[(k+u_C)/(k+u_W)]^n; any fixed premature-coupling hazard changes the large-n limit. Any receipt test has alpha-beta<=TV(P_C,P_W) for its actual observation laws. Clearance of unjoined donors and preservation of registered roots obey a separate wash-time feasibility bound; it does not distinguish stable wrong covalent bonds. Two99% factors multiply to98.01%, not99%, under the declared product model. In a shielded/reactive two-register model, harmless shielded hydrolysis hS cancels from per-encounter wrong/correct odds at fixed other hazards. With immediate independent harmless same-parent replenishment it also cancels from eventual correct-root yield and mean time to any permanent decision. With per-encounter C,W,H,Droot and replacement loss delta, correct-root yield becomes C/[C+W+Droot+delta*H]; successful-recovery time tau changes mean decision time.
